title: Housing billed estimated payroll to a lead-paint grant and returned interest

beats.text: Federal funding was supposed to remove lead hazards from San Francisco homes.

visual.sub: HUD funded lead hazard work in occupied and vacant homes

beats.text: HUD awarded $3 million, with targets for occupied and vacant homes.

visual.kicker: HUD funded lead hazard work in occupied and vacant homes

beats.text: The City reported $877,567 spent under this program in fiscal 2010.
Housing charged salaries and benefits using budget estimates.

visual.kicker: Payroll claims used estimates instead of actual work

beats.text: Auditors wanted records showing the time employees actually worked on the grant.

visual.kicker: Payroll claims used estimates instead of actual work

beats.text: The compliance opinion for this grant was qualified.

beats.text: Housing introduced activity reports for staff working part time on the grant.

beats.text: A separate finding concerned interest on a $300,000 cash advance.

visual.kicker: Housing reported returning interest on a delayed grant advance

beats.text: Housing said project spending took longer than expected.

visual.kicker: Housing reported returning interest on a delayed grant advance

beats.text: The money earned interest that remained unreturned during the audited year.

visual.kicker: Housing reported returning interest on a delayed grant advance

beats.text: Housing later told supervisors it had returned $100.
The final federal decision on payroll costs is still missing.
